headline: Strong freight demand offsets rising claims costs
summary_short: Landstar's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,432.3M, up 18.2% y/y, with diluted EPS of $1.44 (+20.0% y/y), as truck revenue per load climbed roughly 17% and the network added a net 68 BCO trucks, its strongest quarterly gain since Q1 2022.
summary_long: Revenue reached $1,432.3M (+18.2% y/y, +22.3% q/q) on truck revenue per load up ~17% y/y and load volume up ~2%, with truck volumes and rates outpacing normal seasonal demand. Net income rose to $49.0M (+16.8% y/y) and diluted EPS to $1.44 (+20.0% y/y). Higher insurance and claims expense, tied to unfavorable development of prior-years' claims amid a tougher broker-liability claims environment (management cited the U.S. Supreme Court's Montgomery decision), weighed on margins. The Board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.44/share; no shares were repurchased in the quarter. Cash and short-term investments stood at roughly $348M. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Truck revenue per load rose about 17% y/y and truck loads grew about 2%, with network volumes and rates outpacing normal seasonal patterns per management.
Gains were tempered by higher insurance and claims expense, driven by unfavorable development of prior-years' claims amid a tougher broker-liability claims environment.
CEO cited a net 68 BCO truck additions in Q2, the strongest quarterly gain since Q1 2022, as independent contractors returned to the network faster than usual seasonal patterns.
